newsitem.title: USA: U.S. manufacturers wary of rates, dollar - NAPM Ore.
newsitem.headline: U.S. manufacturers wary of rates, dollar - NAPM Ore.

text.p: U.S. manufacturers are most concerned about prospects for higher U.S. interest rates and the impact of a strong dollar on future exports, an official at the National Association of Purchasing Management said.

Asked about the areas of greatest concern for manufacturers, Norbert Ore, chairman of the NAPM business survey committee said that "interest rates ... weak growth abroad, and the dollar impact (on exports)."
Ore spoke to reporters in a conference call following the release of the April NAPM survey, which showed a decline to 54.2 in its main manufacturing index from 55.0 in March.
"There's concern about interest rates and the European economy and the impact we might have later in the year because of either of those," Ore said.
The NAPM official also said manufacturers see "general strength" in the economy, adding that it is still premature to call the drop in the April index a trend.
"I think it would be premature to call that (drop) a trend. Our members continue to indicate that there is strength in their markets," Ore said.
Ore also said employment in the manufacturing sector remained healthy. "I think the employment numbers are somewhat encouraging in the manufacturing sector," he said.
